title: The signal family
summary: Which signal you can answer, what installing a handler takes away, and which connection the close you called did not touch. Getting these backwards is a deploy that takes the full grace period every time, or one that resets live requests.

cards.front: SIGTERM and SIGKILL both end the process. Which one can your code do anything about?
cards.back: SIGTERM. `signal(7)` says SIGKILL "cannot be caught, blocked, or ignored", so when it arrives nothing runs and nothing is flushed.

cards.front: You add a `process.on('SIGTERM')` handler that only logs. What did that one line change about how the process ends?
cards.back: It removed the exit: with a SIGTERM listener installed, Node no longer exits. A handler that only logs leaves a process that has to be killed, so every deploy takes the full grace period.

cards.front: `process.exit()` in the handler, against letting the event loop empty on its own. What does the client see?
cards.back: A reset. Measured on Node 24.16.0 with one request in flight, `process.exit(0)` never delivered the response (`ECONNRESET`), while `server.close()` delivered it in 255ms.

cards.front: The last response went out in 255ms and the process then sat there for six more seconds. What did `server.close()` not do?
cards.back: Revisit a connection that was busy when it was called, so that keep-alive socket waits out `keepAliveTimeout`, five seconds by default. `closeIdleConnections()` reaps them as they free up.

cards.front: The same image stops on your laptop and ignores SIGTERM as PID 1 in the container. What is different about PID 1?
cards.back: It gets no default dispositions: PID 1 only receives signals it has installed handlers for. With no listener SIGTERM does nothing, and the process waits to be killed.

cards.front: `node app.js; echo done` as the container command, against `node app.js` alone. Which leaves node running after SIGTERM?
cards.back: The first: the shell forks node as a child, receives the signal itself and never passes it on. Given a single command, the shell execs node, so node is what the signal reaches.

cards.front: How long does your SIGTERM handler actually have?
cards.back: Not your decision: the window between SIGTERM and SIGKILL is a platform setting. A drain that waits out a five second `keepAliveTimeout` inside a shorter grace period is a kill on every deploy.
